title: Four Knights Game: meeting the Halloween Gambit
line: Seen from Black's side: White gives a knight for a pawn and chases the black knights.

steps.text: The Four Knights Game. Now White gives up its knight on f3 for your pawn on e5.
The Halloween Gambit: a knight for a pawn, to chase your knights with pawns. Engines rate it unsound, and masters almost never play it.
Take the knight. You are a piece up, and White has only a pawn for it.
Step the knight back to g6, near your king and out of reach of the center pawns.
steps.after: The other pawn chases your other knight.

steps.text: Go back home with the knight. You lose time, but you keep the extra piece.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. It gives a pawn back, blocks the bishop for a moment and frees your own.

also.c7c6: That works too: it gets the pawn ready to go to d5. This lesson pushes at once.

steps.after: You have a knight for two pawns. Bring your pieces out and castle, and the extra piece will tell.

summary: Against a gambit that gives a whole piece, take it, step back, and give a pawn back to finish your development.
